real-time RT–PCR.readouts: CHIKV detection and viral RNA copies (viremia, viral titer)

evidence_location.quote: diagnosis of chikungunya was confirmed by real-time RT–PCR in the acute-phase sample

mass cytometry.readouts: immune cell surface marker expression, CHIKV envelope protein E2 expression, canonical leukocyte and sub-community frequencies

evidence_location.quote: Clustering by community frequency revealed a distinct contrast in CD14 + CD16 + monocyte frequencies between the acute and convalescent phases.

multiplex ELISA-based assay (Luminex).readouts: cytokine, chemokine, and growth factor concentrations

evidence_location.quote: The strongest contrast was for the monocyte chemoattractant CCL2 (FDR P = 3.6 × 10 −11 ).

RNA-seq.readouts: gene expression and transcript abundances; differentially expressed genes/transcripts associated with timepoint, viral titer, severity, and antibody titer

evidence_location.quote: We obtained a strong transcriptional signature for timepoint (acute vs. convalescent transcript abundances), with 8,008 transcripts differentially expressed at FDR < 0.05 and FCH > 2 (Fig 6 A).

There was, however, a single significant correlation between CD14 + CD16 + monocyte sub-community 1 at the acute phase and the convalescent anti-CHIKV antibody titer (FDR P = 0.0050, Spearman's ρ = 0.60; see Appendix Fig S3A ).
